entries.082da7db159c49fb: The company mass-processes low-pressure turbine blades for LEAP engines from titanium-aluminum, a material that is hard, brittle and difficult to process.
entries.0dedece9f22d8935: This business uses the technology and experience cultivated in processing titanium aluminide blades, together with Additive Manufacturing (layered fabrication) technology, to carry out contract processing of aircraft engine parts other than for LEAP engines, parts for eVTOL (electric vertical take-off and landing aircraft, so-called flying cars), and parts for gas turbines. For two aircraft engine parts different from the LEAP engine, the company is working on starting volume production at a new factory completed in 2024, and one of them began volume production during the fiscal year ended June 2026. In June 2026, the company acquired all shares of Onoplant Co., Ltd., whose main business is processing aircraft airframe parts and defense-related parts with major Japanese heavy industry manufacturers as its main customers, making it a wholly owned subsidiary, and expanded its business domain to airframe parts and defense-related fields. However, Onoplant is consolidated only on the balance sheet at the end of the fiscal year ended June 2026, and its results are not included in the consolidated statement of income for that fiscal year.

entries.537bb665ad01775a: Operating profit for the fiscal year ended June 2026 was ¥1,145,382 thousand, ordinary profit was ¥1,117,905 thousand, and net income attributable to owners of the parent was ¥781,015 thousand. The annual securities report explains that because materials are supplied free of charge by customers, variable costs are low, and that the profit structure tends to raise profit margins as production and sales volumes increase. At the same time, it states that up-front costs increased, including costs of launching new parts other than for LEAP and costs of expanding staff associated with mass-production development of new materials. Advisory service fees and related amounts of ¥55,200 thousand for the acquisition of shares in Ono Plant Co., Ltd. are treated, on a consolidated basis, as expenses in the period in which they were incurred.
entries.57140935140dddf1: The company has a contract to supply blades for LEAP engines equal to 40% of the total volume required to produce engines for French company SAFRAN. From January 2028, the share is scheduled to change to the high 40% range. The sales performance table shows that sales to Safran Aircraft Engines were 97.0% of revenue for the fiscal year ended June 2026.

entries.6ce25f3f9f12b494: This is the company group's only reportable segment, engaged in the processing, manufacture and sale of aircraft-related parts and other products. The securities report describes the business and its functions in two areas for convenience: "LEAP Titanium Aluminide Blade Processing" and "Other Processing." Net sales in the fiscal year ended June 2026 were ¥5,084,657 thousand, and operating profit was ¥1,145,382 thousand. Because consolidated financial statements have been prepared since the fiscal year ended June 2026, no comparison with the prior period is stated. Most of the sales come from volume processing and sale of titanium aluminide low-pressure turbine blades for LEAP engines to SAFRAN of France. By customer, sales to Safran Aircraft Engines account for 97.0% of sales.

entries.741f7946b9310f03: The [[term:annual-securities-report|annual securities report]] states that the company's group (the company and one consolidated subsidiary) operates a single segment, the Processing Business, engaged in the processing, manufacturing and sale of aircraft-related components and other items. The core business is mass-production processing of low-pressure turbine blades made of titanium aluminum, used in the “LEAP” engines of the French Airbus A320neo family aircraft and US Boeing 737 MAX aircraft. Materials are supplied free of charge by customers, and the annual securities report states that the company bears no working capital burden related to purchasing materials. Sales for the fiscal year ended June 2026 were ¥5,084,657 thousand, the majority of which came from processing and sale of these blades to French SAFRAN. It also undertakes contract processing of aircraft engine components other than LEAP, eVTOL components and gas turbine components.

entries.a5bf885832fb7f90: This business processes and sells titanium aluminide low-pressure turbine blades for the LEAP engine, which is installed on Airbus of France's A320neo family aircraft and Boeing of the United States' 737MAX aircraft; the securities report treats these as the main products. LEAP is an engine developed by CFM International, a joint venture between GE Aerospace of the United States and SAFRAN of France. Titanium aluminide has about half the specific gravity of nickel alloys and is therefore light, but it is hard and brittle and difficult to process; the securities report states that only two companies in the world, including the company, supply titanium aluminide blades for LEAP. Under its contract with SAFRAN of France, the company supplies 40% of the total titanium aluminide blades needed for LEAP engine production, which is scheduled to change to the high 40% range from January 2028. Because materials are supplied free of charge by the customer, the report explains that this is a revenue structure in which the profit margin tends to rise as sales increase. The number of engines fitted with blades sold by the company group in the fiscal year ended June 2026 was 847 (up 32.6% from the previous fiscal year).
